words.intro: Dresden burned in 1945, and its Frauenkirche lay in ruins for fifty years. Today people meet in front of it, a little too early, and look nervously at their phones.

grammar[0].fact: Dresden’s old town has Italian looks, and it was called *Florence on the Elbe* for its art. One thing the Elbe valley no longer has is its UNESCO title: it was removed in 2009 after the city built a new bridge across the view.

grammar[1].blocks[2].title: auf or über?
grammar[1].blocks[2].text: Ich freue mich *auf* das Wochenende — it’s coming. Ich freue mich *über* das Geschenk — I have it now.

grammar[1].fact: German has two words for meeting: *sich treffen* is by plan, *kennenlernen* is for the first time. And a German who says *Wir sollten uns mal treffen* may really mean it, and will ask you which week.

reading.intro: Max has a date, with Sophie from the app. Twenty past seven, in front of the Frauenkirche, in Dresden. He has flowers, and he has been there since six. His phone is on, and Lena is on it.
reading.photos[0].caption: Die Semperoper: Max hat ein Buch darüber gelesen.
reading.photos[1].caption: Die Kasse. Hier wartet man auf seine Karte.
reading.en: Lena: What are you waiting for, Max? You’ve been texting for an hour. · Max: For Sophie. I’m so looking forward to it! She’s interested in music, in art, in old churches. · Lena: And you? You’re interested in football. · Max: Shh. I’ve prepared. I read three books about Dresden. What shall we talk about first? The opera? · Half past seven. No one. Max is annoyed. The flowers are tired already. · Frau: Excuse me, are you waiting for someone too? May I sit here? · Max: Yes, for a woman. She’s very interested in art, poor thing. · Frau: Oh. I’m waiting for a man. He’s interested in art too, he says. I know nothing about it. · Max: Me neither. I’m actually interested in football. · Frau: Really? Me too! I’m Sophie, by the way. · Max: Oh. Hello, Sophie. I’m … the man with the art. · Sophie: Glad to meet you. Nice flowers. When does the match start?
reading.fact: The Frauenkirche collapsed two days after the bombing of February 1945, and the ruin stood as a memorial until 1994. It was rebuilt with money from all over the world and reopened in 2005. The dark stones in its walls are the old ones, back in their old places.
document.caption: Ein Kinoprogramm aus Freiburg, 1993
document.intro: A real cinema listing from a city magazine in Freiburg, June 1993. Many of the films you may recognise under their German titles. Each box gives the cinema first, then the times.
document.fact: German cinemas dub nearly everything, and each major Hollywood star has a permanent German voice: when the same actor dies, fans mourn the voice as well. To see the original, look for *OV* or *OmU*: original version, with subtitles.
